learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the dramatic 18th century where the mighty Mughal Empire declined and vibrant new regional kingdoms rose to power across India!

main_concepts.concept_title: 📉 The Fading Glory of the Mughals
main_concepts.simple_explanation: After the death of Emperor Aurangzeb in 1707, the mighty Mughal Empire began to weaken. Financial troubles, empty treasuries, and weak successors made it impossible to control the vast Indian subcontinent.
As the central power faded, powerful governors broke away to create their own independent states. Places like Awadh, Bengal, and Hyderabad became rich and strong under their new regional rulers.
Groups like the Sikhs, Rajputs, and Jats organized themselves politically and militarily. They fought against the Mughals and carved out their own fiercely independent territories.

By the late 18th century, India was no longer ruled by one single empire. Instead, it was a colorful patchwork of many independent and ambitious regional powers, setting the stage for the arrival of the British.

fun_activity.title: ⚡ Time-Travel Cartographer
fun_activity.instructions: Grab a blank map of modern India and try to sketch where the old kingdoms of Awadh, Bengal, and Hyderabad were located. Notice how state borders have changed today!

quick_recap: ⭐ The decline of the Mughal Empire in the 1700s led to a major power vacuum in India.
⭐ Regional powers like Awadh, Bengal, and Hyderabad became practically independent.
⭐ This divided political map made it easier for European trading companies to slowly gain control.
